Madison County Housing Choice Vouchers: 2,379 people in reported households in 2025
HUD counted 1,057 reported Housing Choice Voucher households in Madison County in 2025.
In Madison County, 2,379 people lived in reported Housing Choice Voucher households in 2025, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
The number of people was down 16 from 2,395 in 2024. Those households numbered 1,057.
HUD reported 1,223 Housing Choice Vouchers available in Madison County, and 88% of those vouchers were in use, up 3 percentage points from 85% in 2024.
HUD said 76% of those households were headed by a person it classifies as a racial or ethnic minority. Households paid an average of $417 a month toward rent and utilities, up $37 from $380 in 2024; their average annual household income was $17,169, up $1,386 from $15,783 in 2024.
Eligible households can use the federal Housing Choice Voucher program to rent privately owned homes. Participants generally pay about 30% of their adjusted monthly income for rent and utilities, and a local housing agency pays a subsidy to the landlord, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. A household may pay more if it chooses a home with rent that exceeds the agency's payment standard.
Families who obtained Housing Choice Vouchers had spent an average of 29 months on waiting lists in 2024, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. The average does not include applicants still waiting or never served; it covers families who received assistance. HUD also estimates that federal rental assistance reaches only one in four eligible families.
